front.title: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Considerations for RATS Evidence and Attestation Results

abstract.t:
The Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) architecture defines Evidence, Endorsements, Reference Values, and Attestation Results as distinct conceptual artifacts used by Attesters, Verifiers, Endorsers, and Relying Parties. The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) raises questions about the protection, validation, transport, transformation, and retention of these artifacts.
This document examines post-quantum cryptographic considerations across the lifecycle of RATS artifacts. It distinguishes post-quantum key establishment from artifact authentication and considers the security properties that must be evaluated independently: integrity, origin, signer authority, freshness, session context, provenance, appraisal, and authorization.
The document introduces three analytical constructs: the Artifact Protection Matrix, the Provenance Continuity Chain, and the Cryptographic Transition Assessment. These constructs provide a structured way to identify artifact-specific protection requirements, evaluate transformations, and preserve the information needed for later cryptographic verification.
The analysis also addresses algorithm selection, cryptographic agility, artifact size, bounded processing, transport considerations, replay resistance, long-term verifiability, interoperability, testing, and privacy.
This document does not define a new cryptographic algorithm, RATS message, token format, transport protocol, TLS extension, key-establishment mechanism, or appraisal-policy language. It provides security analysis and implementation guidance within the existing RATS architecture and established cryptographic standards.
